title: When the Songbook Falls
premise: Tamsin Sterling, a wedding planner who stopped believing in 'I do' after watching his parents' marriage rot behind a flawless facade, treats the heart as a muscle to be trained and contained. Cornered into attending his family's reunion with a plus-one, he hires Delphine Marchetti, a struggling jazz singer who needs rent money, to play the devoted girlfriend for one weekend. But the performance turns real by dessert, and as Delphine's voice — and the truth about why she really needed the money — unravel his defenses, Tamsin must choose between the safe, curated life he's built and a love that demands his whole, unguarded heart, just as Delphine receives an offer to tour abroad that expires the night of the reunion's final toast.
about_author: O. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's happiest days before turning to fiction. They write love stories for people who claim not to believe in them.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. While flawlessly executing a high-society wedding, Tamsin privately dissects love as a trainable, containable muscle, revealing the childhood wound behind his cynicism. A letter from his mother summons him to the family reunion — with a plus-one, or not at all. Emotional beat: controlled detachment cracking under old pressure.

chapters.title: Two Hundred an Evening
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Broke after quitting a demeaning lounge residency, Delphine answers a strange classified ad: actress needed, one weekend, discretion required. She and Tamsin negotiate the terms of a fake relationship with contractual coldness, both convinced they're the smarter one in the room. Emotional beat: wary, transactional sparks.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over one frantic afternoon, Tamsin and Delphine build their shared history — first date, first fight, how they met — and discover an unsettling ease in inventing intimacy. A rehearsal kiss, purely technical, lingers three seconds too long. Emotional beat: the lie starting to feel like a rehearsal for something true.

chapters.title: Arrival at Sterling Hollow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The reunion opens at the family estate, all polished silver and sharpened questions. Tamsin's mother probes; his brother Rhys openly mocks the relationship's authenticity. Delphine improvises brilliantly, but Tamsin notices she's studying his family like sheet music, learning something he'd rather she not see. Emotional beat: performance under hostile lights.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. During dessert, Delphine abandons the script to defend Tamsin against Rhys's cruelty with fierce, unscripted honesty — and the room goes quiet. Walking the gardens afterward, the fake couple has their first real conversation. Tamsin's hand finds hers without a contract requiring it. Emotional beat: the pivot point; the act becomes involuntary.

chapters.title: The Second Verse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Days blur into genuine intimacy: Delphine sings in the estate's empty ballroom, Tamsin confesses why he stopped believing in weddings. But Delphine hides a letter — a touring offer from an overseas jazz collective, acceptance due the night of the reunion's closing toast. Emotional beat: sweetness shadowed by an expiring clock.

chapters.title: What Rhys Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Rhys confronts Tamsin with evidence he's uncovered about the arrangement — and about Delphine's real reason for needing money: her father's debts, and a past entanglement with the Sterling family business. Tamsin, feeling manipulated, retreats behind his old containment, deciding the heart-muscle was right all along. Emotional beat: betrayal, real and imagined, slamming the door.

chapters.title: The Songbook Falls
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Exposed and humiliated, Delphine chooses truth over survival: she tells the assembled family everything — the contract, the money, and the part that stopped being fake the moment dessert was served. She returns the payment, unsigned, and packs to leave before the final toast. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, alone.

chapters.title: The Final Toast
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the closing toast, Tamsin stands before his family and, for the first time, refuses to perform — confessing the arrangement, his own cowardice, and the love he tried to contain. He races to intercept Delphine before her departure, risking rejection with nothing scripted left. Emotional beat: climax; the whole heart wagered, no pieces lent.

chapters.title: An Open Key
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV, closing in Tamsin's. At the train platform, Delphine reveals she turned down the tour before he ever arrived — but needed him to choose her freely, not out of guilt. Months later, Tamsin plans one last wedding: their own, small and unpolished, where he finally believes the words he says. Emotional beat: resolution; the muscle trained at last to open.
